ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a schematic diagram of the motion of Chang'e-3 at a certain stage during its process of flying to the Moon. Chang'e-3 moves along elliptical orbit I to the perilune point P, changes orbit there, and enters circular orbit II. The orbital radius of Chang'e-3 doing circular motion in circular orbit II is r, and the period is T. The gravitational constant is known to be G. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: From the information in the question (including in the figure), the mass of the Moon can be obtained

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, Chang'e-3 moves along elliptical orbit I to the perilune point P and then changes orbit to enter circular orbit II. It is known that the orbital radius of its circular motion on circular orbit II is r, the period is T, and the gravitational constant is G. According to the information in the question (including in the figure), what physical quantity of the Moon can be obtained?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: From the information in the question (including in the figure), the mass of the Moon can be obtained
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the Moon is located inside the circular orbit labeled II, and outside there is also an elliptical orbit labeled I; the two orbits meet at the left-side perilune point P, and Chang'e-3 moves from elliptical orbit I to P and then enters the lunar circular orbit II. Reasoning: The problem gives that Chang'e-3 does uniform circular motion on circular orbit II with orbital radius r and period T, and gives the gravitational constant G. Treat the motion on circular orbit II as the universal gravitational force exerted by the Moon on Chang'e-3 providing the centripetal force, giving GMm/r^2 = m(2π/T)^2 r. Canceling the mass m of Chang'e-3, the mass of the Moon is obtained as M = 4π^2r^3/(GT^2). Therefore, according to the information in the question and the figure, the mass of the Moon can be obtained.
